                Synopsis:
                    US lobbying firms simultaneously represent fossil fuel majors (ExxonMobil, API, ConocoPhillips) and 300+ local governments seeking climate damage funding. Climate superfund legislation — passed in NY and VT, pending in 13 other states — faces organised industry opposition via registered lobbyists. Federal legislation (Stop Climate Shakedowns Act, Cruz/Hageman) seeks to pre-empt state superfund laws. The conflict-of-interest dynamic is systemic, with fossil fuel lobby dollars outweighing public support in legislative outcomes.

                Q01. Is the content relevant to EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
                Relevance: NO — Article is entirely US-domestic in scope, covering US lobbying, US state legislation, and US political dynamics. No direct linkage to EU energy policy, TTF gas, or German power markets.

                Risk score: 15 — The lobbying conflict-of-interest dynamic and fossil fuel industry opposition to climate accountability legislation are broadly known patterns. The specific database findings add granularity but not structurally new risk signals.
